provenance.startWeek: ILLUSTRATIVE: the revised deck's slide 9 shows weeks 41 to 46 of 2026.
provenance.weekCount: ILLUSTRATIVE: twelve weeks in the data (weeks 41 to 52) so a call-off has more than one week to reserve; the board shows the first six by default, as slide 9 draws them.
provenance.keepWeeks: MECHANICAL: week 43 keeps the base scenario's requests and committed orders, which already give 1,800 m3 free and 3,800 m3 wanted (2,000 m3 short, slide 9) with Project A, Contractor B and two float-rich projects competing.
provenance.scriptedWeeks: ILLUSTRATIVE: free capacity and requests chosen so that spare capacity (free minus requested) is +1,200, -700, -2,000, +4,100, +2,500, +1,000 in weeks 41 to 46, the figures drawn on slide 9. Week 42 is short by 700 m3 and week 41's spare covers it by building ahead (slide 9: 'one is already covered by pre-build'). Contractor C's 600 m3 in week 44 is slide 9's second inbox row. Weeks 47 to 52 are a quiet outlook (L3): free capacity of 3,000 to 6,000 m3 and no new requests, so no new shortage appears and slide 9 is unchanged.
provenance.firm.internalShare: ASSUMED: same 40% internal share as the generated scenario (params.json demand.internalShare); only affects the split of already-committed volume.
provenance.firm.splitShares: MECHANICAL: how committed volume is divided among a side's firm orders. No effect on spare capacity.
provenance.firm.internalParties: FICTIONAL: projects that hold the committed internal orders in the scripted weeks.
provenance.firm.externalParties: FICTIONAL: outside customers that hold the committed outside orders in the scripted weeks.
provenance.featuredProject.purchasePriceRM: ILLUSTRATIVE: RM530m is Avantro's GDV (The Edge Malaysia, Sep 2026), used as an upper bound exactly as slide 7's footnote says: 530m x 10% / 365 = RM145,205 a day, the 'RM145k a day' on slides 3, 7 and 9.
provenance.featuredProject.slipDaysPerWeekOfDelay: ILLUSTRATIVE: slide 7 prices Project A at 3 days of slip, 'from the project programme, not the model'. A week's wait is therefore 3 days of handover slip (schedule sensitivity 3/7).
provenance.featuredCustomer.orderValueRM: ILLUSTRATIVE: RM167k is slide 3's and slide 15's illustrative outside order; its margin uses the public 10.8% AAC and precast PBT margin (Q2 FY26), giving about RM18k.
provenance.whatIf.projectId: ILLUSTRATIVE: slide 7's second example gives Project A 20 days of float.
provenance.whatIf.floatDays: ILLUSTRATIVE: 20 days, as slide 7's second example.
provenance.asOf: ILLUSTRATIVE: Monday of week 42, the day slide 10's WhatsApp message arrives (9:42 AM). It fixes what 'next week' means in 'ask the board' (week 43) and which reservations are still active.
provenance.reservations: ILLUSTRATIVE: two reserved slots for projects that confirmed call-offs ahead (slide 7, guardrail 2): 800 m3 in week 45 released on 26 Oct and 500 m3 in week 46 released on 2 Nov unless the call-off is confirmed. They are part of the committed volume, so free capacity still equals slide 9's +2,500 and +1,000 m3.
provenance.reservationPolicy.aheadWeeks: ILLUSTRATIVE: slide 7: 'projects that confirm call-offs 4 weeks ahead get reserved slots'.
provenance.reservationPolicy.releaseDaysBefore: ASSUMED: an unconfirmed reserved slot is released 14 days before its week starts (slide 7 says only that unused slots are released).
provenance.huddle.minutes: ILLUSTRATIVE: slide 11's target is under 30 minutes a week for the decision huddle.
provenance.huddle.blocks: ASSUMED: how the 30 minutes might be split: decisions 15, build-ahead plan 5, slots about to lapse 5, orders to check 5. A pilot would set the real agenda.
provenance.displayWeeks: ILLUSTRATIVE: the board and its chart show the first six weeks (slide 9) unless the visitor asks for more weeks.
